commit.message:
feat(BOU-191): rotate sessions on password + role change (#281)

* feat(security): rotate sessions on password + role change (BOU-191)

Session-management defense-in-depth gap: a password change left older sessions
authenticated, and a role change let a live session retain its old privileges
(invalidate-all-user-sessions was only wired into logout-user-everywhere).

Wire session invalidation into the user service:
- change-password -> invalidate ALL of the user's sessions (a credential change
  forces re-authentication everywhere with the new password).
- update-user-profile -> when :role changes, invalidate the user's sessions so a
  demotion cannot retain elevated access and a promotion starts a fresh session.
  An ordinary (non-role) profile edit does not churn sessions.

Login-time invalidation is intentionally NOT added: multi-device use is
legitimate and session fixation is already prevented by the SecureRandom,
server-minted token (see BOU-168).

Adds a ^:security test asserting invalidation fires on password + role change
and does not fire on a plain profile update; fixes change-password-test's
session-repo stub (previously nil).

Refs BOU-191

* chore(lint): localized ignore for partial session-repo reify in service_test

* fix(security): guard role-change invalidation against partial updates (review)

Only invalidate on role change when the updated entity actually carries :role,
so a future partial update that omits :role is not misread as a demotion and
does not churn the user's sessions. No behaviour change for current callers
(all pass full merged entities).

commit.message:
Add defense-in-depth: invalidate sessions on role/active-status change & block user_type from POST

1. Add Mdl_sessions::invalidate_user_sessions() to destroy all active sessions
   for a user when their role or active status changes, forcing immediate
   revocation of any stale privileged sessions and closing the exploitation window.

2. In Users::form(), block self-privilege-escalation by preventing users from
   changing their own user_type. Explicitly set user_type from POST only when:
   - Creating a new user (allowed)
   - An admin edits another user and the type changes (allowed + sessions invalidated)
   - An admin deactivates a user (sessions invalidated)

3. This removes the vulnerability where POST could directly restore a downgraded
   account's role, and ensures role changes take effect immediately via session
   invalidation rather than trusting permission checks to catch the stale session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
security: revoke sessions when roles change

Advance users.token_version when grant_access changes a role so old privilege-bearing sessions are invalidated while repeated identical grants remain idempotent.

Invalidate sessions when permissions change (fixes stale JWT bug)

Permission changes (per-store overrides, global defaults, bulk push,
reset) now revoke active refresh tokens for affected users. This forces
a re-login with fresh permissions instead of waiting up to 30 minutes
for the access token to expire.

Without this fix, a superadmin could disable transfers for the admin
role but the admin would keep accessing transfers until their JWT
naturally expired.

Affected endpoints:
- PUT /admin/store-permissions → invalidates affected role sessions
- POST /admin/store-permissions/reset → invalidates target role
- PUT /superadmin/permissions → invalidates all users of affected roles
- PUT /owner/store/{id}/permissions → invalidates affected role
- POST /owner/store/{id}/permissions/reset → invalidates target role
- POST /owner/bulk-permissions → invalidates affected roles per store

New helper: invalidate_sessions_for_role(db, store_id, role) in
api/Modules/Auth/Services/principal.py

2255 tests pass, lint clean, frontend builds.

commit.message:
Enforce live database roles and revoke stale sessions

Stage 9: authorize with the current database role and invalidate sessions after security-sensitive user or organization changes.

fix(user): make a system-role change take effect on the next decision

A role change flushed no authz cache and ended no session, so a demoted
administrator kept administrator verdicts for up to the permission
cache's 60s TTL plus a whole access-token lifetime of stale `srole`.

The role branch now does what the deactivate branch does, in the order
that is safe in BOTH directions: write, best-effort invalidate the
user's cached verdicts, end the sessions minted under the old role, then
audit. `user.role.changed` carries `cache_invalidated` and
`sessions_terminated` so an operator can tell "live now" from "live
within the cache TTL" after the fact.

There is deliberately NO refusal, which is where this departs from D27's
original uniform rule (ruling P22/P23 splits it by direction). A role
change is never made safer by refusing it: a refused DEMOTION recreates
this very finding and makes it permanent, and a refused PROMOTION only
delays a harmless stale deny. A failing invalidator, an invalidator
missing from the registry, and a handler with no registry at all are
therefore all reported in the audit row, counted on the cache-invalidation
failure metric, and logged — never turned into a 503.

Session termination is unconditional on a role change and does not
depend on the cache at all; it is the half that retires the stale
`srole` claim. Terminating on every change rather than on demotions
alone keeps one invariant instead of two code paths, and makes a
promotion visible immediately instead of at the next refresh. A patch
that both deactivates and changes the role tears the sessions down once.

`terminateSessions` gains a `...Reporting` sibling that returns the
outcome; the silent form is now a wrapper, so the deactivate and delete
paths are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Also corrects the `iface.AuthzCacheInvalidator` contract comment, which
named this consumer and instructed it to refuse.

Spec 2026-09-03 §4.6 D27 (as amended). Closes M-13.

commit.message:
fix: harden auth — session invalidation on password change + fresh role checks

- Add User.passwordChangedAt; reject JWTs whose iat predates it, so changing,
  resetting, or admin-resetting a password invalidates all older sessions
- Self-service password change now re-issues a fresh token (current session
  survives, other sessions are killed); client adopts it via AuthContext
- Admin password reset stamps passwordChangedAt on the target (revokes the
  affected user's sessions — account-takeover response)
- Switch role-gated admin routes from cached-JWT getUser() to DB-backed
  getUserFresh(), so a demoted admin loses privileges immediately
- (JWT_SECRET rotated out-of-band via gitignored .env, not in this commit)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
